chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn 'Isa and Fadala from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about the Mutamatti' (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu'), when does he visit the House? He said: On the Day of Sacrifice or the next day, and he should not delay it. The Mufrid and the Qarin are not the same; they are given more leeway, in that it is only disliked for the Mutamatti' to delay that (visiting the House) for more than two days, although that delay does not invalidate the Hajj, which indicates that.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One who performs Hajj al-Tamattu' (Umrah then Hajj)
key_terms.الْمُفْرِدُ: One who performs Hajj al-Mufrid (single Hajj)
key_terms.وَالْقَارِنُ: One who performs Hajj al-Qiran (Umrah and Hajj combined)
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: When should a Mutamatti' perform the Tawaf of Umrah during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Mutamatti' should ideally perform the Tawaf of Umrah on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr) or the following day, distinguishing this preference from the Mufrid and Qarin. This ruling highlights the juristic nuance that while delaying beyond two days is merely disliked (makruh) rather than invalidating, the emphasis on promptness reflects the specific ritual structure of the Tamattu' mode of Hajj.
